doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Marit Jerstad and Gurdjieff in Norway
summary: He describes Marit, who introduced him to Gurdjieff, founded the Gurdjieff Foundation in Oslo, and helped get his music on Norwegian television.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: That’s when your good sense kicked in. We were talking about Norway. One of other people who is in that dedication, I think right under Bosse – and I may be mispronouncing it – Marit Jerstad?
Marit was a girl I went with.
You called her the heart and soul of Norway in your dedication. That’s very nice.
Yeah. She was a very strong woman. She introduced me to a man most people may not know, but, Gurdjieff. I don’t know if you’ve heard of Gurdjieff.
Tangerding? I saw a name that reminds me of. Is that Goetz? Or is that someone else? Gurdjieff, did you say?
Gurdjieff.
Was he a Scandinavian also?
No.
A German, or a . . . ?
No, he was from the area we’re fighting today. What is it?
Middle East, there? Persia, Iran, Iraq, Afghanistan?
In that neighborhood.
I see. Gurdjieff? Is that how you . . . ?
Gurdjieff – G-u-r-d-j-i-e-f. There’s a lot of books.
So Marit introduced you to him?
Yeah.
What was . . . ?
She actually started the Gurdjieff Foundation in Oslo.
So this was another person that you knew.
One woman who had worked with Gurdjieff lived in London. She – her name is Miss [Brenda] Tripp. She is 95 or 96 these days. She would come from London to Oslo.
Her name is Miss Tripp?
Marit started the Gurdjieff Foundation in Norway. She also was instrumental in getting the Norwegian television to hear my music and play it.
